pr_title: ini lookup - add case sensitive option
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
<!--- Describe the change below, including rationale and design decisions -->
By setting `ConfigParser.optionxform` to `to_native`, all keys are passed through that function and case is preserved. The [default behavior](https://docs.python.org/3.9/library/configparser.html#configparser.ConfigParser.optionxform) returns a lower case version of the key name rather than preserving the case.

Fixes #74601.
<!--- HINT: Include "Fixes #nnn" if you are fixing an existing issue -->

##### ISSUE TYPE
<!--- Pick one below and delete the rest -->
- Feature Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
`lib/ansible/plugins/lookup/ini.py`
<!--- Write the short name of the module, plugin, task or feature below -->

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Waiting on #74629 before adding tests to avoid merge conflicts and duplicating the test changes already done there.

On Python 2, duplicate key names are silently ignored. If two key names in a section differ only in case, in Python 2 the last one defined in the file would set the value for the key.

issue_context.title: Case sensitive ini lookup option
issue_context.body:
### Summary

When doing a lookup on a java properties file, case sensitivity is being ignored. Since java properties can be used case sensitive this RFE is to have the option to allow a case sensitive lookup on a properties file. 

test.properties
```
fubar=”lower”
FUBAR=”upper”
```
ini_prop_test.yml
```yaml
---
- hosts: localhost
  connection: local
  gather_facts: false
  vars:
    prop_item: "{{ lookup('ini', 'fubar file=test.properties type=properties' )}}"

  tasks:
    - debug:
        var: prop_item

    - debug:
        msg: "{{ item }}"
      with_ini:
        - '.* file=test.properties type=properties re=yes'

...
```
Ansible 2.7.9 Result:
```

TASK [debug] *******************************************************************************************
ok: [localhost] => {

}

}

```

This is more likely due to the Python version change and `ConfigParser` (the library that actually reads the ini) changing behavior after Python 3.2

FYI, after looking at the documentation for ConfigParser, it was always 'case insensitive' the only difference is that since 3.2 they will give you an error.  We can turn the error off, but that won't make the parsing case sensitive, it will just ignore the duplication when using that file.

This is definitely a Python 2/3 difference, not an Ansible version difference. Here is a simple demonstration with the same stack track from the origin report.
```python
from io import StringIO

from ansible.module_utils.six.moves import configparser
from ansible.module_utils.common.text.converters import to_native

u_conf_data = u"""
[section one]
one = one
ONE = two
"""

config = configparser.ConfigParser()
config.readfp(StringIO(u_conf_data))

print(config.get('section one', 'one'))
print(config.get('section one', 'ONE'))
```

```
PYENV_VERSION=2.7.18 python ~/python-files/confparse-case-sensitive.py
two
two

> PYENV_VERSION=3.9.4 python ~/python-files/confparse-case-sensitive.py
/Users/sdoran/python-files/confparse-case-sensitive.py:15: DeprecationWarning: This method will be removed in future versions.  Use 'parser.read_file()' instead.
  config.readfp(StringIO(u_conf_data))
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/sdoran/python-files/confparse-case-sensitive.py", line 15, in <module>
    config.readfp(StringIO(u_conf_data))
  File "/Users/sdoran/.pyenv/versions/3.9.4/lib/python3.9/configparser.py", line 763, in readfp
    self.read_file(fp, source=filename)
  File "/Users/sdoran/.pyenv/versions/3.9.4/lib/python3.9/configparser.py", line 718, in read_file
    self._read(f, source)
  File "/Users/sdoran/.pyenv/versions/3.9.4/lib/python3.9/configparser.py", line 1093, in _read
    raise DuplicateOptionError(sectname, optname,
configparser.DuplicateOptionError: While reading from '<???>' [line  4]: option 'one' in section 'section one' already exists
```


From the [docs](https://docs.python.org/3.9/library/configparser.html):

> strict, default value: True
> When set to True, the parser will not allow for any section or option duplicates while reading from a single source (using read_file(), read_string() or read_dict()). It is recommended to use strict parsers in new applications.
> Changed in version 3.2: In previous versions of configparser behaviour matched strict=False.

The good news is that it seems somewhat trivial to make this case sensitive: we just have to set `ConfigParser.optionxform`. Further investigation is needed to understand the ramifications of that change. I image it will be backwards incompatible as there are probably a lot of people using Python 2 unknowingly relying on this behavior.

```python
from io import StringIO

from ansible.module_utils.six.moves import configparser
from ansible.module_utils.common.text.converters import to_native

u_conf_data = u"""
[section one]
one = one
ONE = two
"""

config = configparser.ConfigParser()
config.optionxform = to_native  # makes keys case sensitive
config.readfp(StringIO(u_conf_data))

print(config.get('section one', 'one'))
print(config.get('section one', 'ONE'))
```

```
> PYENV_VERSION=2.7.18 python ~/python-files/confparse-case-sensitive.py
one
two
> PYENV_VERSION=3.9.4 python ~/python-files/confparse-case-sensitive.py
one
two
```
I made this change and the existing integration tests pass. I'll work on a PR tomorrow with additional tests.

@sdoran making it case sensitive is still not backwards compatible, the `strict` only toggled error reporting, it didn't change case sensitivity. This would be a new feature and I would require a toggle for it.

But your tests suggest the python docs are inaccurate .... so I would try to see if they did actually change that code in python itself or something else is amiss.

> making it case sensitive is still not backwards compatible

Yeah, definitely seems like a new opt-in feature.

> But your tests suggest the python docs are inaccurate .... so I would try to see if they did actually change that code in python itself or something else is amiss.

Supplying duplicate keys still results in the same error. My example had different keys because they were a different case. I don't think we should set `strict=False`. At a minimum we should catch and handle the exception. Maybe we should enable this explicitly so the behavior is consistent between Python 2 and 3? Explicit is better than implicit. But it may not matter at this point since new controller code requires Python >= 3.8.

```python
config.optionxform = to_native
```


Tempted to just add note to the ini plugin docs and describe the diff behaviors observed across pythons, then backport that.

In diff PR add 'new feature' for case sensitivity toggle using your code above, possibly also allow a 'strict' toggle?
@benjdudas Can you test with #74630? I made it work both on Python 2 and Python 3 even though we no longer support Python 2 on the controller.
